To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

::: ::: The more a person trusts the e-vendor, and the more the IT interface is perceived to be useful and easy to use, the more likely it is that the person will purchase from the e-vendor in the future.
Perceived usefulness and ease of use are the most important determinants of trust in the Web site and the vendor, which in turn are the most important antecedents of online shopping behavior."
online trust in an e-vendor is the result of a consumer's beliefs about the e-vendor's honesty, the existence of safety mechanisms, and the ease of using the e-vendor site's interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the factors that lead consumers to trust e-vendors and to engage in online shopping.
the antecedents of trust and its impact on the use of online shopping Web sites.
the development of an integrated model of online consumer trust and TAM in an e-vendor setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trust in the vendor is the most important factor that determines online shopping intentions.
trust in online vendors is built through the interaction with both the vendor and its Web site interface.

the TAM model is not sufficient to explain online shopping, that it must be supplemented by an examination of trust in the online vendor and its Web site interface, and that the trust-building mechanisms are different from those that build trust in other environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trust in the online vendor is built by the consumer's perception of a safe and easy to use Web site interface.

online trust is a function of the e-vendor's reputation, of the perceived security of the Web site, of the ease of use of the Web site's interface, and of the perceived ease-of-use and usefulness of the IT itself.
online trust is a complex construct that is built through multiple mechanisms, and that online trust is an essential antecedent to purchase intentions in online commerce.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Web site interface and the e-vendor are both important in the development of consumer trust, and that trust is a critical determinant of online purchase intention.
the Web site interface is a significant factor in building consumer trust.
the IT interface itself can be an important factor in building trust in online shopping, and that trust in the IT is as important as trust in the vendor in determining consumer purchase intentions.
